description:
Move the claim and confirmed-delete cases that only the exit-code suite tests into the claim and issue-lifecycle suites.

## Background

`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/exit_code_tests.rs` (39 subprocess tests) re-proves projected exit codes and also owns behaviour no other test owns. The exit-code projection suite owns command-to-exit-code bindings and their human/machine parity: outside it, a subprocess test asserts success or failure and the property it adds, and names a numeric exit code only for a command and code pair the projection has no row for. This entry covers these cases:

- `:652`, `:702` and `:765`: claim and claim-next blocked by dependencies or a precheck gate, with `BLOCKED` details and remediation.
- `:820`: claim-next skipping non-ready issues.
- `:897` and `:920`: blocked-claim messages naming `--assign`, human and JSON.
- `:954` and `:999`: an assign-only claim sets the assignee without a transition, and claiming a ready issue moves it to in-progress.
- `:1590` and `:1616`: confirmed delete in text mode ("Deleted issue:") and JSON mode. These strings appear in no other test.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each claim case listed in the Background has an owning test in `cli_repo_workflow/claim_integration_tests.rs`, and each confirmed-delete case has one in `cli_repo_workflow/integration_test.rs`, with the same non-exit assertions.
- [hard] REQ-02: A moved case names a numeric exit code only where the projection has no row for its command and code.
- [hard] REQ-03: A behaviour an existing test in those files already owns is not duplicated.
title: Claim and confirmed-delete cases move beside their owners
